responsibility.value: Removes the global Bearer security requirement from OpenAPI operations that do not need authentication, based on endpoint metadata inspection.

Owns: Clearing operation.Security to an empty list when the endpoint carries [AllowAnonymous]
Clearing operation.Security to an empty list when the endpoint carries neither [AllowAnonymous] nor [Authorize] (fully public endpoints)
Leaving operation.Security untouched (global Bearer requirement applies) when the endpoint has [Authorize] without [AllowAnonymous]
doesNotOwn: Adding the global Bearer security scheme (owned by BearerSecurityTransformer, a separate document-level transformer)
Actual runtime authorization enforcement (handled by ASP.NET Core's AuthorizationMiddleware, not by OpenAPI transformers)
Determining which specific roles or policies are required (delegated to [Authorize(Roles=...)] attributes on controllers)

collaborators.detail: Implements the single-method interface that the ASP.NET Core OpenAPI infrastructure invokes per-operation during document generation
Reads context.Description.ActionDescriptor.EndpointMetadata to inspect endpoint-level authorization attributes
Checked via metadata.Any(m => m is IAllowAnonymous) to detect anonymous endpoints and clear their security
Checked via metadata.Any(m => m is IAuthorizeData) to detect authorized endpoints — absence triggers security clearance for public endpoints
Sets operation.Security = [] to remove the global Bearer requirement from anonymous or public endpoints
Received as a parameter in TransformAsync; its Description.ActionDescriptor.EndpointMetadata is read to inspect auth attributes

contracts: After TransformAsync for an endpoint carrying [AllowAnonymous], operation.Security is an empty list (global Bearer requirement suppressed)
After TransformAsync for an endpoint with no [Authorize] and no [AllowAnonymous] metadata, operation.Security is an empty list
After TransformAsync for an endpoint carrying [Authorize] but not [AllowAnonymous], operation.Security is left unchanged (the Bearer requirement from the document-level transformer remains)
If EndpointMetadata is null or empty, both metadata.Any() calls return false, so the second branch fires and clears security — treated as a public endpoint
assumptions: No other IOpenApiOperationTransformer will re-add security to an operation after this one clears it — branch 2 (no IAuthorizeData) does NOT return early, so a later transformer could re-instate the Bearer padlock on a public endpoint

Any endpoint authorization mechanism implements IAuthorizeData — if a custom auth filter does NOT implement IAuthorizeData, the transformer treats the endpoint as public (documentation inaccuracy, though actual request-time auth still applies)
invariants: Endpoints with [AllowAnonymous] always have operation.Security = [] regardless of [Authorize] presence at controller or action level (the IAllowAnonymous check returns early)
All decisions are purely metadata-driven — no connection strings, no external configuration, no runtime state is consulted
failureModes: Documentation inaccuracy: endpoints secured by a custom authorization filter that does not implement IAuthorizeData appear as unauthenticated in the Swagger/Scalar UI (branch 2 fires even though the endpoint is actually protected at request time)
Fragile ordering: if a later IOpenApiOperationTransformer runs after this one and re-adds security, public endpoints acquire a spurious Bearer padlock in the UI
architecturalNotes: Logical asymmetry between branch 1 and branch 2: branch 1 returns early after clearing security (defensive against later transformers), but branch 2 does not — the inconsistency is harmless today but fragile under future extension
Documentation-layer only — does not affect actual request authorization; only controls what the Swagger/Scalar UI displays to API consumers
